data.scope: Final-step damage aggregation has a conservative eligibility guard. protocol.decision_rule: Exploratory fixed-size screen only. A lower paired 95% score bound above 0.5 warrants a separately prespecified fresh confirmation; otherwise do not claim superiority or extend this sample. No adoption from this 64-game screen.
protocol.scope: Game-derived full-tree own-history information correction; native timed comparison against local default search, not an optimality proof or deployed-binary/human comparison. Both private split log branches retained. Wall-clock runs are not exactly reproducible.

null.scope: Prespecified 64-game exploratory timed comparison, 32 side-swap blocks, 500 ms per non-forced search including construction, continuation setup and log generation but excluding observation/sync and destruction. Total choose times also recorded. Common seeds do not make wall-clock runs exactly reproducible. The identical-agent null is a separate fixed-3000-iteration test. This is a local default comparison, not deployed binary superiority, human calibration or a game-optimality certificate. No adoption from this screen.

summary.scope: Prespecified 64-game exploratory timed comparison, 32 side-swap blocks, 500 ms per non-forced search including construction, continuation setup and log generation but excluding observation/sync and destruction. Total choose times also recorded. Common seeds do not make wall-clock runs exactly reproducible. The identical-agent null is a separate fixed-3000-iteration test. checks.decision: Won more games than lost but failed the prespecified superiority screen; no additional matches or adoption of this implementation. Investigate the measured history/log cost before any new candidate.

summary.scope: Exact compact lookup for the same own full-history policy. Transition hashes select collision chains, then compare full parent, action, request and protocol lines. Action lists are compared within each history. Copies occur only on insertion; identical IDs and bandit statistics are preserved. Native sequential measurements include construction and search. The first pass rotates four modes but always runs legacy_shared before compact_shared; a second pass balances those two orders within each root. Repetitions use identical seeds, not independent games. Stored byte counts include protocol string contents in both prefix records and index keys, not total resident memory. This measures cost and identity, not strength or game-optimality.

order_confirmation.order: legacy/compact, compact/legacy, legacy/compact, compact/legacy within each root

summary.decision: No sampled hidden-roster payoff variation in this screen; do not deepen this sample to diagnose hidden-roster loss.
summary.scope: 24 hash-selected own-side decisions from 62 eligible one-survivor-per-side decisions in the frozen 24-game corpus. Each model has 16 equally weighted draws from the current belief, with the Quick Claw coin averaged exactly before opponent responses. Opponent knows its sampled type; own root policy is common to all types. One decision-step enumeration retains nonterminal and unexpanded mass as [0,1]. Bounds apply only to this finite sampled model, not the entire prior or all legal unseen rosters. No terminal value is assigned to truncated play. Matrix strategy brackets are independently recomputed with rational arithmetic on recorded floating-point masses. All samples happen to have identical lower/upper payoff tables within each root; this fails to expose hidden-roster payoff uncertainty and does not establish that true opponents have no hidden alternatives. One 27000-iteration normal search seed per root is diagnostic, not a full-game strength result. Engine and belief semantics remain trusted.

summary.decision: Deprioritize this witness for large strength gains; its security ceiling is below 0.11 percentage points.
summary.scope: Reuse the validated, same-observation Fire Blast/Growl Marowak counterexample. The lower certificate mixes Double Edge and Earthquake before the simultaneous choice and follows the archived Double Edge priority; it is valid against every response in those two roster worlds only. The upper certificate uses the legal Growl roster and randomizes two fixed opponent policies, Earthquake priority and Growl then Earthquake. Their full reply certificates cover all four own first actions and arbitrary later replies. The opponent chooses its policy before seeing the own random action. Thus the upper bound also limits security against any larger unseen-roster set containing this verified Growl world. It is not a Bayesian bound for a prior assigning this world negligible or zero probability. Linear envelopes are optimized and checked with exact rational arithmetic on archived conservative floating-point bounds, then padded by 1e-8. Historical engine certificates and public-history replay are reverified without rewriting their source hashes. This bounds one adverse decision, not average match improvement, occurrence frequency, or global distance to optimality.

Single unrevealed-move substitutions by moves with an explicit Generation 2 machine source and native format acceptance. Other slots, items, stats and roster entries are unchanged. Each alternate team passes the native flat validator; adding a Generation 2 machine move introduces no new egg or event combination constraint. Every prefix is replayed from the initial teams with full logs, own observations and legal actions equal. If the original unseen move was silently selected, the alternate selects its replacement. The census is restricted to both sides having one survivor in a fixed 24-game corpus. The follow-up screens every accepted variant at roots whose original one-step guaranteed score lower exceeds 0.01; omitted roots can still hide large losses because partial enumeration and future play are unresolved. Each two-world game uses a common own mixed action and lets the opponent choose its world and reply before seeing the own random choice. The hidden Quick Claw coin is averaged before that response. All nonterminal and unexpanded chance mass stays [0,1], with 128 engine-run enumeration caps. Matrix bounds are independently checked with rational arithmetic on recorded floating-point probability masses. These are finite two-world security diagnostics, not average win rates, the whole legal roster universe, or a claim that zero detected loss proves optimality. Current normal search uses its unchanged catalog belief and one 27000-iteration seed per root. No human calibration.

The least-overlapping unresolved one-step candidate among the 89 candidates whose lower-optimal policy beats the normal chosen action on lower payoffs. Same public history, both one-survivor teams; replace unseen Zapdos Rest with format-legal Generation 2 TM Hyper Beam. Root sleep duration is held at the native replay value in both worlds; other unseen legal rosters and sleep durations are not covered. Fixed own Rock Slide and Swords Dance then Rock Slide policies provide attainable lower bounds. A fixed opponent sequence of Sleep Talk, Sleep Talk, Hidden Power Ice provides upper bounds against all own actions and later replies. That sequence depends only on decision count and own legal actions, not the observed own random choice or future hidden state. Counterpolicy ledgers and all chosen policy actions are independently checked; unexpanded/horizon mass remains [0,1]. The two-world robust optimum is bracketed by a single shared Rock Slide policy and the Hyper Beam world counterpolicy. These conditional security scores are not a Bayesian-prior optimum or average match win rate. Normal belief remains unchanged; pinned true-roster searches are oracle diagnostics, not deployable information. Sixteen search seeds are repetitions at one decision, not sixteen games. Native engine semantics and guarded-state equivalence remain trusted. No human calibration or production change.

A fixed replayed Zapdos/Marowak endgame with three revealed Zapdos moves and one occupied unknown slot. Enumerate all 39 remaining move names from the native format learnset at level 50, excluding duplicate Thunderbolt, Sleep Talk and Hidden Power. Sources include Generation 1/2 machines and level moves; the three retained moves are machine/tutor moves and introduce no egg/event compatibility dependency. Native team validation and every public-prefix/own-action check are performed by the unchanged census harness; the certificate harness separately replays all 38 alternatives and checks logs and observers. Stats, items, occupied move count, current sleep duration and all other state are fixed; the full game information set is not covered. One common Rock Slide priority supplies the family lower bound. A fixed precommitted Sleep Talk/Sleep Talk/Hidden Power Ice opponent sequence in the limiting world supplies an upper bound against all own first actions and adaptive later replies. Fixed policies depend only on decision count and legal actions. Partial enumeration and horizon leaves keep [0,1] bounds. Ledger arithmetic and every policy action are checked independently. Rest certificates are reused without rewriting their historical hashes; Hyper Beam certificates reproduce exactly. These are conditional security values, not a prior-weighted win rate. Positive per-world losses are initial-action certificates assuming optimal subsequent play. Changing the initial action is not a uniform improvement: it provably sacrifices value in some worlds. No production change, human calibration, wall-time speed claim or deployed-bot superiority claim.

searches.scope: The highest certified Swords Dance loss in the archived 39-move family. Sixteen search seeds at this single decision; native default belief in both same-observation worlds, plus pinned true-roster oracle controls. All original-world rows reproduce the earlier archive exactly. Normal rows are identical across worlds. Losses use the independently certified Reflect-world first-action bounds with optimal later play, not sampled battle outcomes. Pinned results use unavailable roster knowledge and are not a deployable fix.
